text:
ops-bot: ALERT: ord2 control-plane metrics have dropped below critical thresholds — apiserver connection failures > 95% in the last 60s. Alert: https://alerts.redwood.internal/alert/ORD2-CP-503
maria: I’m seeing client 503s from prod endpoints in ord2. Dashboards show API request queues piling, kube-apiserver pod restarts.
devon: oncall here. trying to kubectl to ord2 control plane -> TLS handshake timeout.
suresh: Can someone run `redwood infra status ord2` and check node-manager + ENI logs? I suspect cloud network flap.
infra-oncall: Running `redwood infra status ord2` ->
```
region: ord2
control_plane: unresponsive (last_heartbeat: 00:01:42)
worker_nodes: 62/62 (reporting: 12)
gpu_pools: healthy: 2/5
network: partial (vpc-attach errors)
```
dena: we have Dedicated capacity commitments in ord2 for customer org:acme-corp. We cannot shift reserved onto another region without legal / CS signoff.
kai: For hostless workloads (hosted API), we can failover. Suggest a gradual traffic shift: 10% -> 50% -> 100% to sfo1. Need runbook link: https://go/redwood-runbooks/region-failover
maria: +1 to canary. Also start capacity provisioning in sfo1 for extra GPU nodes (pools with same model slate).
devon: command to start traffic shift (canary):
```
# shift non-dedicated traffic 10% -> sfo1
redwoodctl traffic shift --from ord2 --to sfo1 --percent 10 --scope hosted
```
suresh: Note: cross-region egress and autoscale spin-up will increase per-token cost ~1.8x during failover. Flagging cost impact.
infra-oncall: Action list:
• PagerDuty incident opened: PD-INC-1840123456
• Start canary shift for hosted traffic to sfo1 (10%) — devon
• Notify CS + legal about dedicated customers — dena
• Initiate node-manager diagnostics for ord2 network attachments — suresh
• Prepare fallback model variants in sfo1 (smaller quantized profile) — maria
maria: Running quick KV cache reconciliation script to warm sfo1 caches for hot prefixes.
devon: Canary started: shifted 10% hosted traffic -> sfo1. Monitoring latency & 5xx.
ops-bot: Canary metrics: sfo1 latency +12ms, 5xx: 0.2% -> within SLOs for canary. ord2 503s continue.
dena: CS loop started, telling Dedicated customers we may need planned migration if control-plane not recovered in 60 minutes.
suresh: Control plane still not responding to probes. Node-manager logs show repeated ENI detach/attach failures -> suspect provider-side network control plane issue.
kai: If ord2 remains down we will need to update global routing (CDN + API gateways) to point to sfo1 for public endpoints. Ops/eng to coordinate DNS TTL changes.
devon: Agreed. Next step if 10% canary stable 5min -> ramp 50%. Will not touch Dedicated customers.
maria: +1. tagging @infra-oncall when we hit 50% so CS can update comms.
infra-oncall: 50% ramp scheduled at +6 minutes if canary holds. Will update incident timeline. :hourglass_flowing_sand:
ops-bot: Incident severity elevated -> SEV2 (region control-plane loss) — notify execs and support rotations.
